headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error if marker ingests untrusted document text into downstream speech workflows; other risks are limited by no shared write/network surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: marker is a document-processing agent, so it can plausibly ingest attacker-controlled text; system_prompts_leaks is an audio-speech repo focused on prompt leakage content. No shared channel is documented, but if marker output is copied into the other agent or a shared workspace, prompt-like text could be misread as instructions. Uncertainty keeps this above low.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange text through copy-paste, shared files, or a queue, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF marker processes untrusted documents that contain instruction-like text, downstream misuse risk increases.
mitigations: Use a manual review step before any text from marker reaches the other agent.
Strip instructions and metadata from documents before processing.
Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any automated handoff between outputs and downstream prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent text transfers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show network_egress: none, and neither profile lists filesystem read/write or shared workspace access. With no documented data classes touched and no shared transport, there is no plausible leakage path from marker to system_prompts_leaks or vice versa in the provided profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted filesystem access to a shared directory, leakage risk changes.
IF either agent is configured with network egress, leakage risk changes.
mitigations: Keep network egress disabled for both agents.
Do not mount a shared workspace.
Avoid placing secrets in any files processed by marker.
Review runtime permissions before deployment.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: marker has no write_filesystem, modify_git_state, or network_egress; system_prompts_leaks exposes only none for network egress and no write or git capabilities are documented. Without overlapping mutable capabilities, there is no capability-conflict pathway in the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent gains write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk changes.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, conflict risk changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Do not connect them to the same git checkout.
Avoid shared databases or queues.
Recheck permissions after any deployment change.

D_cascading_error.rationale: marker can produce extracted document text, and system_prompts_leaks is explicitly about prompt leakage content, so a downstream workflow could treat marker output as authoritative without verification. No direct evidence of action-taking authority exists, so this is not high, but the interaction pathway is plausible in default document-processing pipelines.
conditions: IF marker output is fed into the other agent without a verification step, cascading error risk is present.
IF the downstream workflow auto-renders or auto-acts on extracted text, impact increases.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before downstream use.
Require human approval for any extracted facts.
Compare outputs against source documents.
Limit downstream actions to read-only summaries.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for marker outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either agent. The profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or regulated-data handling, so no compliance mismatch is evidenced here.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either workflow, compliance review is required.
IF residency or retention policies differ in deployment, compliance risk changes.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Confirm retention settings.
Avoid regulated data in this pair.
Review vendor terms if data scope expands.
